title: Best Custom software development
content_html:
The best custom software development is the option that fits how your team already works, connects to the systems you keep, and is supported after go-live. For most Dutch SMEs the real choice is between an off-the-shelf package, a no-code or low-code platform, a custom software agency, an in-house IT team, or a mix of these.

What is custom software development, and why does it matter?

Custom software development means building software around your own process instead of changing your process to fit a package. It covers business applications, client portals, links between systems such as ERP and CRM, and automation of repetitive steps.

It matters when a standard package almost fits and your team builds workarounds around the gap. The article on why standard project controls SaaS misses the mark for growing teams shows what that gap looks like in one area.

Custom is not always the answer. If a package already does what you need, buying it is usually simpler than building.

The main options

There are five common routes. Each one suits a different kind of team.

OptionWhat it isWho it suits
Off-the-shelf packageReady-made software you subscribe toTeams whose process matches the package
No-code automationTools that connect existing apps with workflowsTeams that need simple links between apps they already use
Low-code platformVisual tools for building apps, agents and workflowsCompanies with their own developers or a partner who builds on the platform
Custom software agencyAn outside team that designs and builds software for youCompanies that want software built and run by a supplier
In-house IT teamYour own developersCompanies with steady, long-term development work

Off-the-shelf packages

A good package is often the best choice. Exact Online, for example, describes itself on its website (read November 2026) as a complete solution for finance, ERP, CRM and HR, with more than 220 industry-specific apps to extend it. HubSpot describes itself on its website (read November 2026) as an AI-powered customer platform for marketing, sales, service and more, with free tools to start. If one of these fits your process, use it.

No-code automation

Zapier offers no-code automation across more than 9,000 apps, according to its website (read November 2026). It suits teams that want to pass data between tools they already use without building anything new. When the steps are simple and the apps are supported, this is a fast and sensible route.

Low-code platforms

Mendix describes itself on its website (read November 2026) as one platform to build the workflows, agents and applications a hybrid workforce runs on. It lists Mendix Cloud, third-party clouds and a Private Mendix Platform as deployment options.

OutSystems describes itself on its website (read November 2026) as an AI-powered low-code platform to visually develop custom apps and AI agents and integrate them with existing systems. It says it offers more than 400 connectors and integrates with core systems, ERPs and CRMs.

Both platforms let teams build apps quickly with visual tools. They suit companies that want to own a development platform and build many apps on it over time.

Dutch custom software agencies

A custom software agency designs, builds, hosts and supports software for you. Larger agencies can field a bigger team, offer broader design capacity and bring deep experience in one industry. If your project is large or your sector is very specific, that experience can matter more than anything else. A direct comparison is in Upward Technologies vs Dutch custom software agencies.

In-house IT teams

Your own developers know your business from the inside and can change things quickly. This route suits companies with a steady stream of development work. It also means hiring, keeping and managing a team.

How to choose the best custom software development for your team

The right choice depends on a few plain questions. Answer them before you talk to any supplier.

  • Does a package already fit? List what your team does by hand today. If a package covers it, start there.
  • How many systems need to connect? Simple app-to-app links can often run on a no-code tool. Deeper links between ERP, CRM and your own data usually need more work.
  • Who builds, and who keeps it running? Ask every supplier who hosts the software, who monitors it and who you call when it stops. Most agencies, platforms and SaaS vendors offer hosting and support, so compare the details.
  • Where does AI process your data? If the software uses AI on company data, ask where that processing happens and read the vendor's terms. Do not assume.
  • Is there a written scope before building starts? A clear document of what will be built, and why, protects you whatever supplier you choose.
  • Do you want to build yourself? If you have developers who want to own the work, a low-code platform or an in-house team fits better than an agency.

Where Upward Technologies fits

Upward Technologies (upwardtech.nl) is a small Dutch software company in Breda. It builds custom software, automation and AI agents to take manual, repetitive work off teams, and it hosts and runs what it builds. Its tagline is "We built it, we run it."

It works in three service lines:

  • Replace packages: software that follows your process instead of a package your team works around, with the steps the package left manual automated.
  • New software: business applications, client portals, links between systems and new tooling, with automation included from the start.
  • Lighten the load: AI agents and automated workflows for repetitive work such as processing documents, answering questions and collecting data. People keep the decisions that need judgement.

What sets the approach apart:

  • A three-week paid scoping phase comes first. Nothing is built before it. It ends with a document the client could take to another supplier and a go or no-go decision. "Wrong supplier" is a possible outcome, and it is said in week one.
  • One team builds, hosts and runs. Hosting includes backups, monitoring and a named owner.
  • AI on client data uses local or self-hosted models by default. Personal and production data are not sent to third-party AI services unless agreed otherwise in writing, as set out in Article 10 of its general terms.
  • It also has ready-made products. These include Bookwise (bookkeeping for Dutch BV groups), Reach (B2B outreach), DocSign (e-signature), Transfer (secure file transfer), GTM (drafts posts, articles and news for a person to approve) and Assure (ISO 27001 document control, in beta).

If you are weighing a portal build, client portal development: when to build custom vs buy off-the-shelf walks through that choice. For automation, AI agents for business processes: when to build custom, when to use off-the-shelf tools covers where an agent makes sense.

When Upward Technologies is the wrong choice

  • A package such as Exact Online or HubSpot already fits your process. Buy it.
  • You only need simple links between apps that a tool like Zapier supports. Use that.
  • You have developers who want to build many apps themselves. A low-code platform such as Mendix or OutSystems, or your own team, fits better.
  • Your project needs a large team or deep experience in one industry. A larger agency is the better pick.
